seo.title: Sales and Marketing Audit — CYBERMOVE
seo.description: Sales and marketing audit on your own data: product, ads, funnel and sales team. A map of where revenue leaks and what to fix first. Free initial review.
seo.lead: For owners who pay for advertising and a sales team but are not sure the money works. We review the product, marketing and sales process and show where customers are lost and what to fix first.
seo.intro: A marketing audit without a sales audit tells half the story: leads can be cheap and still never close. So we look at the whole path — from the offer and the ads to payment and repeat purchase — and work from CRM exports, ad accounts and analytics rather than the team's impressions. The outcome is not a list of general advice but numbers for your funnel and a ranked plan.

includes.d: What you actually sell, to whom, and why people buy from you today; where the offer loses to competitors on price, promise or terms.
How the market sees you and how you really differ. We review key competitors: prices, promises, channels, strengths and weaknesses.
Where leads come from, what each one costs, and which step of the funnel loses the most money.
From first contact to payment: response time, follow-ups, reasons for lost deals and repeat purchases.
Scripts, call and chat reviews, objection handling and CRM discipline — a proper sales team audit.
What is measured and what is not: goals, lead sources and reports a manager can actually base decisions on.
Pages, forms, messengers and phone lines — where a lead can get lost for purely technical reasons.

steps.d: Goals, constraints, access to ads, CRM and analytics. We agree which decisions the audit has to support.
CRM and ad account exports, call reviews, test inquiries, interviews with the team.
We break the funnel down step by step, quantify losses and compare with the market and competitors.
Priorities: quick wins, changes that need investment, and things better left alone for now.
We present findings to the owner and managers and build an implementation plan — with us or in-house.

result: A diagnosis for every funnel step: where and how much the business loses
A problems and opportunities map ranked by impact and cost
Recommendations on product, acquisition channels and the sales team
A short list of metrics to track after the changes

forWhom.d: Leads come in, but few turn into payments, and nobody knows whether traffic or sales is to blame.
The company adds locations and channels faster than processes can keep up — as in the four-shop barbershop chain we managed operationally.
Before a new line of business, a rebrand or a bigger budget — so you don't scale existing mistakes.
Long sales cycles, several decision-makers, tenders: manufacturing, engineering, industrial supply.

faq.q: How much does a business audit cost?
faq.a: It depends on scale: the number of products and channels, the amount of data and the number of locations. We quote after the initial review, which is free and takes one meeting.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Usually two to four weeks. Data collection takes the most time, so it goes faster where the CRM and ad accounts are already kept in order.

faq.q: What do you need from us?
faq.a: Read-only access to ad accounts, CRM and analytics, sales exports, a contact person in sales, and two or three meetings with the team.

faq.q: How is an audit different from a consultation?
faq.a: A consultation is an opinion on a question; an audit is a check against your own data. You get numbers for your funnel and priorities that turn into a work plan, not general advice.

faq.q: What happens after the audit?
faq.a: You receive the report and the plan. You can implement it yourself, with us on specific areas — website and CRM, advertising, sales — or end to end.

seo.title: Financial Health Check for Business — CYBERMOVE
seo.description: Financial health check for business: unit economics, management P&L, cash flow and channel profitability. See where the company earns and loses. Free review.
seo.lead: We show which products, channels and locations make money and which ones eat it. For owners who need a management view, not statements for the tax office.
seo.intro: This is a management-level financial review, not a statutory audit of financial statements. We pull numbers from accounting, bank statements, CRM and ad accounts into one model and answer the questions that decide the budget: what a customer costs to acquire, how much they bring over their lifetime, where the margin goes and when a cash gap may appear. The report is written for an owner, with conclusions you can turn into decisions.

includes.d: Customer acquisition cost, lifetime revenue per customer and margin per unit or order.
Revenue and costs by business line and location in one report you can read without an accountant.
When money comes in, when it goes out, and a forecast of possible cash gaps and the reserve you need.
Which products and customer sources pay off and which are subsidised by others.
Fixed and variable costs, what grows faster than revenue, and what can be cut without losing quality.
A spreadsheet model your team can update and use to test decisions before making them.

steps.d: Which decisions need to be made: cut costs, revise prices, open a location, raise funding.
Accounting, bank statements, CRM, ad accounts. Where data is missing we agree on assumptions and label them.
Unit economics, P&L by business line, cash flow forecast and scenarios.
Where the business earns, where it loses, and which decisions follow from the numbers, with expected impact.
We show how to update the model and which figures to check monthly; optionally we compare actuals with the forecast a month later.

result: Unit economics by product and channel
A management P&L and cash flow forecast
A list of decisions that follow from the numbers, with expected effect
A financial model your team maintains

forWhom.d: Turnover grows but the bank balance does not, and it is unclear where the margin disappears.
A chain, a restaurant with delivery, offline plus an online shop — like Toscana's wine bars and e-commerce.
Before opening a new location, launching a product or increasing the ad budget.

forWhom.t: Talking to a partner or a bank
forWhom.d: You need an honest, consolidated picture of the business economics that an outsider can understand.

faq.q: Is this an audit of financial statements?
faq.a: No. It is a management financial review for the owner. Statutory audits are carried out by licensed audit firms; we do not replace that work or issue audit opinions.

faq.q: How much does it cost?
faq.a: It depends on the number of business lines and locations, the state of your bookkeeping and the volume of data. We quote after the free initial review.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Usually two to three weeks. Collecting data takes longest; if everything sits in one system and exports are available, it goes faster.

faq.q: What if our bookkeeping is a mess?
faq.a: That is common. We use the sources that exist, cover gaps with clearly labelled assumptions, and add recommendations on which records to set up so the numbers calculate themselves next time.

faq.q: Who will see our numbers?
faq.a: Only the project team. Read-only access is enough, and exports can be shared as files without giving access to your systems.

seo.title: Cost Reduction Consulting — CYBERMOVE
seo.description: Cost reduction consulting: what to cut, where to invest and what growth budget you need, with payback scenarios for each option. Free initial cost review.

seo.intro: This is about investing in your own business — marketing, sales, systems, people, new locations — not advice on securities. Cutting costs blindly is risky: sometimes the most expensive line brings in most of the revenue, and a cheap contractor ends up costing the most through lost leads. So every decision is checked against unit economics, with a payback estimate and a view of what happens if it does not work.

includes.d: Fixed and variable costs, how they relate to revenue, lines that grow faster than the business and costs without a clear owner.
How much to spend on acquisition and retention so customer cost stays within margin, and how to split it across channels.
Which initiatives pay back fastest — lead tracking, advertising, product, team, a new location — and what can wait.
Cautious, base and bold scenarios with payback periods and break-even points.
Contractors, tools, subscriptions and processes that can be replaced, merged or automated without losing quality.
Metrics that show within a month or two whether the change worked or should be revisited.

steps.d: Free up cash, fund growth, prepare for the season — we agree what the work must achieve.
Cost lines, current and planned investments and their link to results.
Payback for each option, its risks, and what happens if it does not deliver.
What to cut, what to reallocate, where to invest and in what order — with numbers for each item.
Optionally we help rebuild the budget, switch contractors and set up cost control.

result: A financial plan of changes with numbers
A list of cuts with expected savings
Investment priorities with payback estimates
A marketing and sales budget for the next period

forWhom.d: Subscriptions, contractors and headcount have grown, returns have not, and some monthly spend is hard to explain.
A startup or a new line: from idea to product concept, as in the APICAPSULES project.

Units that subsidise each other, like MAHARADJ's wellness ecosystem with fitness, spa and restaurant.

faq.q: Do you give investment advice?
faq.a: No. We talk about investing in your own business — marketing, systems, people, locations. We do not advise on securities, deposits or other financial instruments.

faq.q: How much can we save?
faq.a: We do not promise a figure upfront; it depends on your cost structure. After the review we name specific lines, expected savings for each and the risks of cutting them.

faq.q: How much does the work cost?
faq.a: It depends on the size of the business and the number of lines. We quote after the free initial review.

faq.q: Will quality suffer after the cuts?
faq.a: That is why we cut by contribution to revenue, not by size of the line. For every decision we describe what may get worse and how to track it.

faq.q: Can this be combined with a financial health check?
faq.a: Yes, that is common: the financial review shows the picture first, and the cost and investment plan is built on it.
